info.title: Neuro & Evil Karaoke API
info.description:
The API behind the Neuro & Evil Karaoke web player at [neurokaraoke.com](https://neurokaraoke.com),
[evilkaraoke.com](https://evilkaraoke.com) and [twinskaraoke.com](https://twinskaraoke.com). 

**Base URL:** `https://api.neurokaraoke.com`

## Authentication

Most read endpoints are public. Endpoints marked with a lock need credentials, passed in one of
these ways:

| Method | Example |
| --- | --- |
| Bearer token **recommended** | `Authorization: Bearer YOUR_TOKEN` |
| Guest ID | `X-Guest-Id: ANY_UUID` |

The karaoke site lets visitors who are not signed in add songs to playlists, play games and more.
Those requests are tied to a guest ID instead of an account. Send the same UUID every time to keep
the guest's data.

To get a token, sign in with one of the endpoints under **Authentication**, or copy the
`authToken` value from the karaoke site's local storage. Paste it into the authentication panel
without the `Bearer ` prefix. This page fills in a guest ID for you.

## Status codes

| Code | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `200` / `204` | Success |
| `400` | The request is missing a value or has an invalid one |
| `401` | Missing, invalid or expired token |
| `404` | The item does not exist |
| `429` | Too many requests. Wait a moment before trying again |

## Webhooks

Get notified when a karaoke setlist is added or updated.

TBD

## Other documents

Listen along and radio chat use WebSockets, and the 24/7 radio runs on AzuraCast. Each has its own
document. Pick them from the document selector at the top of the sidebar.

get.description:
Returns a page of fan art, as shown on the art gallery page. `page` starts at 1. `pageSize` defaults to 30 and accepts 1 to 200 (values outside that range fall back to 50).

`search` matches the credit, description, file name, tags and artist. `tag` takes one or more tag names separated by spaces, and every tag must match. `artistId` limits results to one artist (IDs come from `GET /api/media/artists?loadArts=false`). `hideWebM=true` leaves out animated WebM files.

`sort` accepts `newest` (the default), `oldest`, `score_desc` or `score_asc`.

The response has `items`, `totalCount`, `page` and `pageSize`.

Authentication is optional. When a bearer token is supplied, the request is associated with that user.

Returns every fan artist. With `loadArts=true` (the default), each artist also includes all of their art.

**Large payload:** with `loadArts=true` the response contains every artwork on the site and can be several megabytes. Pass `loadArts=false` when you only need the artist list.

Authentication is optional. When a bearer token is supplied, the request is associated with that user.

post.summary: Sign in with username and password
post.description: Validates the username and password and returns a bearer token. Usernames are case-insensitive. Returns `400` when the request is malformed and `401` when the credentials are wrong or the account is locked. Requests are rate limited per client.

Creates a QR sign-in session for the calling device. No request body.

The response contains `sessionId`, `approveUrl` (the URL to encode in the QR code), `qrCodePayload` (same value), `qrCodeImageDataUrl` (a ready-to-display PNG data URL), `statusStreamUrl` and `expiresAt`. Display the QR code, then wait for approval with `GET /api/auth/qr-session/{sessionId}/events` or by polling `GET /api/auth/qr-session/{sessionId}`.

Treat `sessionId` as a secret. Anyone who has it can collect the token after approval.

get.description: Returns the status of a QR sign-in session. `status` is `pending` until the user approves, then `approved` with the bearer token in `token`. Returns `404` when the session does not exist or has expired. When polling, wait at least 2 seconds between requests.

Server-Sent Events (`text/event-stream`) alternative to polling. Each event's `data` is a JSON object with `Status`, `Token` and `ExpiresAt`. Note the PascalCase property names, which differ from the camelCase names returned by the status endpoint. The stream sends the current status immediately, sends a heartbeat comment every 15 seconds, and closes after the `approved` event or when the session expires. Returns `404` (as JSON) when the session does not exist.

post.description:
Called by the signed-in user's device after scanning the QR code. Approves the session in `sessionId` and hands the caller's sign-in to the waiting device. Returns `404` when the session is invalid or expired. Clients should always ask the user to confirm before calling this.

**Requires a bearer token.**

Creates a 6-character login code for the signed-in user. No request body. The code is valid for 5 minutes and can be redeemed once with `POST /api/auth/redeem-code` on another device. Codes use uppercase letters and digits and never contain the ambiguous characters `0`, `O`, `1` or `I`.

**Requires a bearer token.**
Exchanges a login code for a bearer token. `code` is case-insensitive. Returns `404` when the code is invalid, expired or already used. Requests are rate limited per client.

Authentication is optional. When a bearer token is supplied, the request is associated with that user.

Starts today's session for the caller and records the start time. Each caller can play once per day. Returns 409 if today's game was already completed. Set `excludeFromLeaderboard` to play without affecting rankings. `mode` selects the challenge variant. Defaults to Normal.

**Requires a bearer token or an `X-Guest-Id` header.**

get.summary: Get the clip for an attempt
get.description:
Returns the audio clip for an attempt (1 to 6). Later attempts return longer or less distorted clips.

With a bearer token, only clips for attempts already played and the next attempt are returned. Call `/start` first. A later attempt returns 400. All clips unlock once the game is finished. `mode` selects the challenge variant. Defaults to Normal.

tags.name: Password sign-in
tags.description:
Sign in with a neurokaraoke.com username and password. Use this when the client has a keyboard and the user is comfortable typing their password into it.

Every sign-in flow ends with a JWT that is sent as `Authorization: Bearer <token>` on later requests. Tokens are not refreshed, so sign in again when a request returns `401`. Store tokens in the platform's secure storage and never log them.

tags.name: QR code sign-in
tags.description:
For devices with a screen but no convenient keyboard (TVs, desktop apps, kiosks). The user approves the sign-in from a phone that is already signed in.

1. The device calls `POST /api/auth/qr-session` and displays the returned QR code.
2. The device waits for approval through `GET /api/auth/qr-session/{sessionId}/events`, or polls `GET /api/auth/qr-session/{sessionId}`.
3. The user scans the QR code on a signed-in phone and confirms. The phone calls `POST /api/auth/approve-qr`.
4. The device receives `status = approved` together with the bearer token.

Sessions expire after 5 minutes. Create a new session when the old one expires.

tags.name: Login code sign-in
tags.description:
For car head units (Android Auto, CarPlay) and other devices where scanning a QR code is impractical. The user reads a short code from a signed-in device and types it on the new device.

1. On a signed-in device, call `POST /api/auth/pairing-code` and show the 6-character code to the user.
2. The user enters the code on the new device, which calls `POST /api/auth/redeem-code`.
3. The new device receives a bearer token.

Codes expire after 5 minutes and can be redeemed only once.

tags.name: Karaoke setlists

tags.name: Genres, themes and moods
tags.description:
Lookup lists used for song filters (genres, themes, moods, artists, cover artists, languages, stream dates) and the detail pages for a single genre, theme or mood.

The `/api/filters/*` endpoints share the same parameters: `search` (case-insensitive substring), `page` (zero-based, default 0) and `pageSize` (default 50). The returned IDs can be passed to the song search filters.

tags.name: Bandle challenge
tags.description:
Daily song-guessing challenge. Expected call sequence:

1. `GET /today` returns the current challenge metadata.
2. `POST /start` starts the session and records the start time.
3. `GET /audio/{attemptNumber}` returns the clip for the current attempt.
4. `POST /attempt` submits a guess or a skip. Repeat steps 3 and 4 until the song is guessed or attempts run out.
5. `POST /complete` finalizes the result.

Session endpoints require either a bearer token or an `X-Guest-Id` header. Guest results are
recorded but are not included in leaderboards.
